CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sarah is a 27-year-old female here for her annual visit. She reports she has been doing better overall but has been struggling with depression, particularly off and on over the past year due to being trapped inside and working remotely. She is currently taking Prozac 20 milligrams daily and feels the medication has helped her in the past. She states a lot has been weighing on her lately and thinks increasing her dose might help her through this difficult period. She also reports chronic back pain that she has been managing. The pain bothers her when sitting for long periods at her desk at work but improves when she gets up and moves. She experiences some numbing in her extremities but denies tingling or pain down her legs. The symptoms improve with position changes and standing. She denies leg weakness. She reports that the back pain affects her when she is on her feet for too long as well as when sitting too long. She is able to perform activities of daily living including exercise and shopping. She has a history of coronary artery bypass grafting at a young age due to a congenital coronary artery. She reports her heart has been doing well and her arteries have been looking good.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for numbing in extremities. Negative for tingling in legs, pain down legs, or leg weakness. Able to perform activities of daily living.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, chronic back pain, congenital coronary artery, coronary artery bypass grafting

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20 milligrams daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works at desk. Exercises. Shops independently.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Does not appear in distress. Neck: No thyroid enlargement. Heart: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable. Lungs: Clear. Abdomen: Soft. Lumbar spine: Pain on palpation, decreased flexion. Lower extremities: Good strength, no edema.

RESULTS
EKG: Basically unchanged from last year. Lumbar spine X-ray: Stable from last year.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Depression: Increase Prozac from 20 milligrams to 40 milligrams once daily. Prescription to be sent to pharmacy. Chronic back pain: Referral to physical therapy. Pain medication offered but patient declined physical therapy as preferred initial approach. Cardiac: Order echocardiogram. Continue aspirin 81 milligrams daily. Nurse will assist with scheduling follow-up appointments.
